text:
jess: customer acme-inc opened a support ticket — they keep getting 429s even though Console shows ~50k tokens available for their org in the past 24h. they pasted a sample request id.

jess: repro steps:
1) curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-ACME' -d '{\"input\":\"hello\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
2) see 429 response with body: {\"error\":{\"type\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\",\"message\":\"quota exceeded\",\"code\":429}}

jess: sample request id: req_acme_0a1b2c3. customer says Console token panel shows plenty remaining at that minute.

lucy: thanks — can you drop the API response headers (x-request-id, x-enforcer-key, x-enforcer-window?) and the console snapshot link?

jess: headers: x-request-id: req_acme_0a1b2c3, x-enforcer-key: acct:acme:global, x-enforcer-window: 1678886400-1678887000. console snapshot: https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/acme/usage?ts=2111113333 (screenshot attached).

quota-aggregator-bot: alert: consumer-lag(quota-aggregator)=7300 messages; last-commit-offset=9823421; latest-offset=9830721.

samir: interesting. our enforcer uses per-request sliding token windows and reads current token state from the token-store. Console uses the rollup pipeline (quota-aggregator) to build time-bucketed totals. if the aggregator is lagging, Console can appear stale/under-report.

mike: i pulled enforcer logs around req_acme_0a1b2c3 — it did enforce and return 429. enforcer debug shows tokens_left=0 at enforcement_time.

jess: so enforcer correct, console stale. customer upset because UI said they had quota. need to explain.

samir: digging deeper: aggregator consumer restarted at 21:01 UTC due to OOM. on restart it skipped a small partition range due to a bug in our commit-offset logic. that left ~30k events unprocessed for acct:acme for the past 15m. the consumer-lag metric matches that.

samir: quick repro commands:
```
kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --describe --group quota-aggregator
kubectl logs -l app=quota-aggregator -c aggregator | grep acct:acme -n
```

samir: logs show repeated serialization-error when processing event id e12345, then consumer crashed and on restart commit pointer jumped, skipping the bad batch.

lucy: that would cause Console rollups to miss those increments, making Console undercount usage (so Console shows more remaining). weird that Console would undercount instead of overcount — but yes if events never made it into the rollups, Console wouldn't reflect the usage that enforcer already applied.

mike: action items:
- samir: run a targeted backfill for acct:acme from kafka offsets 9828000-9830000 and repair rollups.
- samir: add fix for commit-offset-on-crash bug (PR opened).
- lucy: draft customer explanation + transient timeframe to expect corrected numbers.
- jess: offer customer temporary bypass? (they ask for relief)

samir: backfill job queued, ETA ~45m. PR for commit fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quota-aggregator/pull/451.

jess: i'll tell the customer we found an ingestion gap causing the Console snapshot to miss ~15m of usage; the enforcer was correct to throttle. proposing a credit and a postmortem.

mike: also adding a monitor: alert when consumer-lag > 5m AND unprocessed-events-for-populated-orgs > 10k. putting runbook steps in oncall doc.

infra-bot: deploy status: quota-aggregator/backfill-job started (job id backfill-2111113333-1). logs: https://infra.redwood.ai/jobs/backfill-2111113333-1

lucy: thanks everyone. i've opened support ticket #SUP-4822 and customer-facing note drafted. will update once backfill completes.

jess: backfill finished — infra-bot logs show successful rollup repair. customer confirmed 429s stopped after token counters reconciled. closing loop; will watch the monitor for 24h. :white_check_mark:

mike: follow-up: schedule postmortem and invite infra+enforcer+console owners.

jess: adding notes to #incidents and creating a short postmortem.
